intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of witnessing the phenomenon. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir area, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Book the Comfort package for towel, drink, and mask included. A bucket-list hot spring experience unlike any other.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, dating back to 1891, surrounded by geysers and hot springs bubbling nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the dramatic ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves of Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Learn about Iceland's volcanic geology and climate change impacts while experiencing one of the country's most iconic landscapes up close.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught fish, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,500 ISK) to Reykjavik city center. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront accommodation. Take a short orientation walk along the nearby coastline to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the famous Reykjavik Old Harbour area for a relaxed first evening stroll. Watch for the northern lights after dark from the beachfront — January skies offer excellent aurora viewing opportunities. Dress in all available warm layers and scan the horizon after 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane
meals.lunch: Grab a budget hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's most famous hot dog stand, under 600 ISK, a true local institution
meals.dinner: Hlöllabátar (Subway-style Icelandic sandwiches) in Reykjavik city center — filling and budget-friendly at around 1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January in Iceland means very short daylight hours (roughly 5–6 hours). Temperatures hover around -2°C to 4°C. Layer up immediately upon arrival. Download the Vedur app (Icelandic Met Office) for real-time aurora and weather forecasts. Exchange some currency or confirm your card works for tap payments — Iceland is nearly cashless.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church (free exterior, 1,000 ISK for tower access) and enjoy panoramic views of Reykjavik and the surrounding snow-covered landscape. Walk down Skólavörðustígur street, browsing local shops and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjavik City Pond (Tjörnin) — completely free and beautiful in winter with possible ice and visiting birds. Walk to the Harpa Concert Hall to admire its stunning geometric glass facade from outside (free). Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) for insight into Viking-age Reykjavik — around 2,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the beachfront area near the hotel for dedicated northern lights watching. The Grótta lighthouse peninsula, just west of Reykjavik, is one of the best light-pollution-free spots near the city. Bundle up and stay out for 1–2 hours after 21:00 if the KP index is 2 or above.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the hotel — pick up supplies from Bonus supermarket (Iceland's cheapest grocery chain) including skyr, bread, and fruit for under 1,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Cozy bowl of Icelandic lamb soup (Kjötsúpa) at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — approx. 1,800 ISK, warming and traditional
meals.dinner: Self-catered pasta or noodle meal using Bonus supermarket ingredients — budget approx. 800–1,200 ISK total

day_by_day.notes: Bonus supermarket is your best friend for budget travel in Iceland. Stock up on breakfast and snack items to significantly cut daily food costs. The Grótta lighthouse area is a 25–30 minute walk from central Reykjavik or a short bus ride on Route 11.

day_by_day.morning: Take the public Strætó bus (Route 1 or organized tour) toward the Golden Circle. First stop: Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá canyon rift for free. Stunning in winter with frost and ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Geysir Geothermal Area — completely free to visit. Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Walk the steaming geothermal field carefully. Then visit the majestic Gullfoss waterfall (free entry) — partially frozen in January and absolutely spectacular.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik by late afternoon/early evening. Stop at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir if timing allows — one of Iceland's most affordable natural hot spring pools at around 3,000 ISK. Soak under the dark winter sky with possible aurora views overhead.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel — skyr with granola and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, and thermos of hot coffee or tea to enjoy at Geysir
meals.dinner: Upon return to Reykjavik, grab a budget kebab or burger from a city center takeaway — approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is best done via a guided budget tour (approx. 7,000–9,000 ISK) or by renting a car shared among travelers. Public buses do not cover the full Golden Circle route efficiently in winter. Book in advance. Dress in waterproof outer layers — Gullfoss spray can drench you even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (Grasagarðurinn) — free entry and eerily beautiful in winter frost. Then walk to Perlan, the futuristic glass dome building. The outside observation deck offers stunning 360° views over the city and coast (free). The Wonders of Iceland museum inside costs around 2,900 ISK but includes a real indoor ice cave.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach — a unique man-made geothermal hot tub and warm sandy beach area right on the ocean. Entry is free or minimal cost (around 400–800 ISK seasonal). Soak in the warm geothermal water while looking out at the cold Atlantic Ocean — a surreal Icelandic experience.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavik's Laugavegur main street for window shopping and street culture. Check aurora forecast — if KP index is favorable, head to Öskjuhlíð hill behind Perlan for unobstructed dark sky northern lights viewing away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Noodle soup or bowl from a budget Asian restaurant in Reykjavik city center — approx. 1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using hotel kitchen facilities if available, or pick up ready meals from Bonus — budget 1,000–1,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Nauthólsvík Geothermal Beach has limited winter hours — check the official Reykjavik city website before visiting. The water temperature in the lagoon area is around 15–19°C year-round thanks to geothermal mixing. Bring a towel and swimsuit.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Reykjanes Peninsula — take a budget rental car or join a small group tour. Visit the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the Mid-Atlantic Ridge rift. Walk across two tectonic plates for free. Explore the dramatic volcanic lava fields of the Reykjanes UNESCO Global Geopark.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Gunnuhver hot spring area — one of Iceland's most powerful geothermal areas with massive mud pools and steam vents (free). The sulfuric steam and boiling mud are dramatic and otherworldly. Drive to the Reykjanes Lighthouse on the southwestern tip — beautiful coastal views and crashing winter waves.
day_by_day.evening: Stop at the Blue Lagoon area on the way back — note that entry to the Blue Lagoon itself is very expensive (25,000+ ISK), but you can view it from outside for free and enjoy the surrounding lava field landscape. Return to hotel and check aurora forecast for late-night viewing from the beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus — thermos soup, sandwiches, and snacks enjoyed at Gunnuhver with dramatic steam backdrop
meals.dinner: Fish and chips from a budget Reykjavik chippy or takeaway — approx. 2,000–2,500 ISK, try fresh Icelandic cod

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula suffered significant volcanic activity in 2023–2024 — check current geological safety advisories before visiting certain areas. The Bridge Between Continents is located near Sandvík and is signposted from Route 425. Free parking available.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Elliðaárdalur valley — a beautiful free nature reserve within Reykjavik city limits. Walk along the frozen river and through birch forest. Look for Arctic birds including redwings and snow buntings. This hidden gem is rarely visited by tourists and offers a peaceful winter wilderness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Árbæjarsafn, the Reykjavik Open Air Museum — a collection of historic Icelandic turf houses and buildings showing traditional life. Entry approx. 2,200 ISK. Afterward, visit the Laugardalur geothermal valley — the site of Reykjavik's main public swimming pool (Laugardalslaug) for a budget hot spring soak at only 1,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Laugardalslaug public pool has outdoor hot tubs at various temperatures (38–44°C) and is open until 22:00. Soak in the naturally heated geothermal water under the dark winter sky — northern lights visible directly from the hot tubs on clear nights. This is one of the best budget aurora + hot spring combinations in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Café at Árbæjarsafn museum serves traditional Icelandic food — try skyr cake and coffee for around 1,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Reykjavik Chips (Frítúruhúsið) — legendary Icelandic fries with various toppings, very affordable at 1,200–1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug is Iceland's largest public swimming pool and a true local experience. Strict shower rules apply (shower naked before entering). Bring your own towel and swimsuit or rent them for a small fee. This is where locals go — far cheaper and more authentic than the Blue Lagoon.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget day tour or rental car to the South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk behind the cascading water (free, though icy in January — exercise caution). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall (free) — climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views over the coastal plain.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the black sand beaches of the South Coast. Visit Reynisfjara black sand beach near Vík — one of the most dramatic beaches in the world with basalt column formations and sea stacks (free). WARNING: Never turn your back on the ocean here — sneaker waves are extremely dangerous. View from a safe distance.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Dyrhólaey peninsula viewpoint (free) for views of the iconic rock arch and puffin cliffs (no puffins in January but the scenery is stunning). Return toward Reykjavik. Stop at a roadside viewpoint for northern lights if forecast is good — the South Coast has minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus consumed at Skógafoss — hot soup in a thermos is essential
meals.dinner: Upon return, budget pizza slice or wrap from a Reykjavik takeaway — approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 2.5–3 hours each way from Reykjavik. Start early to maximize the limited 5-hour daylight window. Roads can be icy — rent a 4WD vehicle and check road.is for current conditions before departure. Budget tour operators like Extreme Iceland or Gray Line offer South Coast day tours for approx. 8,000–11,000 ISK.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long South Coast day. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely self-catered breakfast, and do laundry if needed. Visit a local Reykjavik café for a warming coffee and to plan the week ahead. Browse the Kolaportið flea market (open weekends) for cheap souvenirs and local snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn Íslands) — entry approx. 2,500 ISK, covering 1,200 years of Icelandic history from the Viking settlement to modern day. Excellent exhibits on Norse mythology, medieval manuscripts, and traditional crafts. Very warm inside — perfect for a cold January afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to Tjörnin pond at dusk for beautiful blue-hour photography. Then head to the Sundhollin public pool in central Reykjavik — a gorgeous Art Deco building with outdoor geothermal hot pots open until 22:00. Entry approx. 1,200 ISK. Soak and relax under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a café breakfast — try Sandholt Bakery for fresh Icelandic pastries and coffee, approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.lunch: Self-catered from Bonus supermarket
meals.dinner: Mandi restaurant — excellent budget Middle Eastern food in Reykjavik, shawarma plates approx. 1,800–2,200 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Kolaportið flea market is only open on weekends (Saturday–Sunday, 11:00–17:00). If Day 8 falls on a weekday, substitute with the Culture House (Safnahúsið) which has free entry to certain exhibitions. Sundhollin is located on Barónsstígur street in central Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Snæfellsnes Peninsula — rent a car or join a budget group tour. Drive through the dramatic lava fields of Berserkjahraun. Visit Búðakirkja, the iconic black church standing alone against the volcanic landscape (free, exterior).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snæfellsjökull glacier and national park — the glacier that Jules Verne used as the entrance to the center of the Earth. Walk the free coastal trails around Arnarstapi and Hellnar with stunning basalt arch formations and bird cliffs. Visit Vatnshellir lava tube cave — guided tours approx. 3,000 ISK and absolutely worth it.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Kirkjufell mountain — the most photographed mountain in Iceland, shaped like a church steeple. The adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall is stunning. This area has very low light pollution — excellent northern lights territory. Stay until 21:00–22:00 if aurora forecast is favorable before returning to Reykjavik.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel before early departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from Bonus — this is a long driving day so roadside picnic stops are necessary
meals.dinner: Late dinner back in Reykjavik — Noodle Station for warming ramen-style noodle soup, approx. 1,500–1,800 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 2.5–3 hours from Reykjavik. The full peninsula loop is about 200km. A 4WD vehicle is strongly recommended. Budget group tours to Snæfellsnes run approx. 9,000–13,000 ISK. Check road.is before departure — Route 54 and 574 can be icy or closed.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik's 101 district on foot — visit the colorful corrugated iron houses, street murals, and independent bookshops. Stop at the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavíkur) — three venues, entry approx. 2,200 ISK for all. The Hafnarhús building near the harbour has rotating contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free coastal walking path along the Sæbraut seafront — stretching from the Sun Voyager sculpture (Sólfarið) westward. The Sun Voyager is a stunning Viking longship sculpture and one of Reykjavik's most iconic landmarks — free to visit and photograph. Continue to Grótta lighthouse at the end of Seltjarnarnes peninsula for coastal bird watching and aurora potential.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated northern lights hunting evening. Join a budget aurora hunting tour by minibus (approx. 5,000–7,000 ISK) — guides drive away from city lights to the darkest available sky and have aurora expertise. Most tour operators offer a free repeat tour if no lights are seen. Book through Local Guide or Arctic Adventures.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Icelandic hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur again — a classic worth repeating, under 600 ISK
meals.dinner: Pre-tour early dinner — Aktu Taktu fast food restaurant in Reykjavik, burgers and fries approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The northern lights aurora tour is highly recommended for at least one evening during the trip. Professional guides monitor the KP index and cloud cover in real time and drive to optimal viewing locations. The best aurora months in Iceland are October–March. A clear sky with KP index 3+ gives excellent viewing chances.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Geothermal Exhibition at Hellisheiði Power Plant (Geothermal Energy Exhibition) on the outskirts of Reykjavik — entry approx. 1,500 ISK. Learn how Iceland harnesses volcanic energy for nearly all its electricity and hot water. The surrounding Hengill volcanic area has beautiful steaming vents visible from the road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Hveragerði — Iceland's 'hot spring town' just 45 minutes from Reykjavik. The town sits on a massive geothermal field with hot springs in people's gardens. Walk the free geothermal park in the town center. Hike up the Reykjadalur valley trail (approx. 3km each way) to the famous hot spring river where you can bathe in naturally warm flowing water — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavik. Visit the Laugardalslaug public pool one more time for a relaxing evening soak in the outdoor hot pots. Reflect on the trip so far and plan final days. Check aurora forecast for late-night viewing from the hotel beachfront.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hotel
meals.lunch: Packed thermos lunch for the Reykjadalur hike — hot soup and sandwiches essential in January cold
meals.dinner: Skál! Kitchen and Bar in Reykjavik — affordable Icelandic comfort food, mains approx. 2,500–3,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hot spring river hike is one of the best free experiences in Iceland. The trail starts at the Hveragerði campsite parking area. In January the trail can be icy and snowy — wear hiking boots with microspikes if available. Water temperature in the river varies — find a comfortable spot. Bring a towel and change of clothes in a dry bag.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite Reykjavik spots. Morning walk along the beachfront near the hotel to appreciate the dramatic winter coastline. Visit the Reykjavik Maritime Museum (Sjóminjasafnið) near the Old Harbour — entry approx. 1,800 ISK. Explore the harbor area and watch fishing boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Vesturbæjarlaug public pool — a quieter, more local alternative to the larger pools. Outdoor geothermal hot pots at 38–44°C, entry approx. 1,200 ISK. Spend a long, leisurely afternoon soaking and chatting with locals — this is quintessential Icelandic culture. Afterward, pick up final souvenirs from the Bonus supermarket (Icelandic chocolate, dried fish, and licorice are affordable gifts).
day_by_day.evening: Final northern lights attempt — take a taxi or walk to Öskjuhlíð hill or Grótta lighthouse for one last aurora hunt. If lights appear, this will be a magical farewell to Iceland. Celebrate the trip with a slightly splurged dinner at a mid-range restaurant. Pack bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a final proper Icelandic breakfast — Gló restaurant offers healthy Icelandic bowls from approx. 2,000–2,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Self-catered from Bonus — use up remaining groceries
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on a farewell meal — Hamborgarabúllan (The Tommi's Burger Joint) for excellent Icelandic burgers, approx. 2,500–3,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to pick up duty-free allowances if needed. The Kringlan or Smáralind shopping malls have larger stores if you need any last-minute gear or gifts. Confirm your Flybus transfer to the airport for tomorrow — book online for the cheapest rate (approx. 3,500 ISK). Set an early alarm for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. Enjoy a relaxed self-catered breakfast using any remaining hotel supplies. Take one last walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to the Atlantic Ocean and the Icelandic landscape. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and arrange luggage transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if afternoon/evening flight, store luggage at the hotel or at Reykjavik BSÍ bus terminal (approx. 800 ISK per bag). Visit the Harpa Concert Hall interior (free) for a final look at its stunning geometric architecture. Walk the Old Harbour one last time. Take the Flybus to Keflavik International Airport (journey approx. 45–50 minutes — depart at least 2.5 hours before flight).
day_by_day.evening: At Keflavik Airport — browse the duty-free stores for affordable Icelandic spirits, chocolate, and skincare products (often cheaper than city shops). Board your flight home with memories of hot springs, northern lights, volcanic landscapes, and the unique magic of Iceland in winter.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered final breakfast at hotel — use up all remaining food supplies
meals.lunch: Light meal at Keflavik Airport — airport food is expensive, so bring snacks from the hotel. Budget 2,000–3,000 ISK if buying at the airport
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Flybus departs from Reykjavik BSÍ terminal and also picks up from many central Reykjavik hotels — confirm your pickup point when booking. Allow extra time in January for potential road delays due to weather or ice. Keflavik Airport has excellent facilities including a geothermal hot tub viewing area (Sky Lagoon is nearby but expensive). Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before departure. Total estimated budget for 13 days excluding flights and accommodation: approx. 80,000–110,000 ISK (€550–€750) covering transport, activities, meals, and pool entries.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of witnessing the phenomenon. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir area, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Book the Comfort package for towel, drink, and mask included. A bucket-list hot spring experience unlike any other.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, dating back to 1891, surrounded by geysers and hot springs bubbling nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavik International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 45–60 min drive depending on location).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your beachfront room. Take a leisurely coastal walk along the shoreline to get oriented, breathe the crisp Arctic air, and admire the dramatic winter seascape. Visit the hotel's amenities and plan your upcoming days with the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Head out for your first Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a small-group guided tour into the dark Icelandic countryside away from light pollution. January offers long dark nights and excellent aurora viewing windows. Wrap up warm and enjoy the spectacle if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport upon arrival (e.g., Keflavik Airport café — budget around 1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Light meal at the hotel restaurant or a nearby café after check-in — try Icelandic fish soup (kjötsúpa) for a warming welcome.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant before the evening jeep tour. Opt for a classic Icelandic lamb stew or pan-fried Arctic char. Budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pack all cold-weather layers for the evening Northern Lights tour — temperatures in January can drop to -5°C to -10°C. The jeep tour typically departs around 21:00–22:00 and lasts 3–4 hours. Aurora activity depends on geomagnetic conditions and cloud cover — the guide will choose the best location on the night.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booking essential). Arrive early to enjoy the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters in the mystical winter morning light. Indulge in an in-water silica mud mask and mineral-rich soak. The Blue Lagoon is conveniently located near Keflavik, making it easily accessible from the resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Blue Lagoon, drive or take a short transfer to the Reykjanes Peninsula to explore the dramatic lava fields and the Bridge Between Continents — a footbridge spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Visit the Gunnuhver hot spring geothermal area with its powerful steam vents and bubbling mud pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a rest before another Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep. The Reykjanes Peninsula's remote coastline offers great dark-sky spots. Alternatively, check aurora forecast apps (e.g., Vedur.is) and if conditions are excellent, step outside the hotel for a spontaneous viewing session on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — typically includes skyr, smoked salmon, rye bread, and eggs. Budget around 2,500–3,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Blue Lagoon's Lava Restaurant or grab a simpler meal from their café counter. Budget around 3,000–5,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near the resort or in a nearby town. Try Icelandic lamb burger or bacalao (salt cod). Budget around 3,500–5,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon tickets must be pre-booked online — standard entry starts around 9,990 ISK. Bring a hair tie as the silica can tangle hair. The spa provides towels and silica masks. Gunnuhver is free to visit but stay on marked paths as the ground is geothermally active.

day_by_day.morning: Drive the Golden Circle route — depart early to maximize Iceland's limited winter daylight (roughly 5–6 hours of light in January). First stop: Þingvellir National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates meet. Walk the Almannagjá rift valley and learn about Iceland's ancient parliament.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to the Geysir Geothermal Area — witness Strokkur geyser erupting every 5–10 minutes, shooting boiling water up to 40 meters high. Then drive to the magnificent Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in winter, creating a breathtaking icy spectacle. Explore the viewpoints along the canyon.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward the resort. On the way back, stop at a local pool or hot pot if one is en route. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and, if the aurora forecast is favorable, step outside or join a spontaneous viewing session on the hotel beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet before an early departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a café near Geysir — Geysir Center has a café with soup, sandwiches, and hot drinks. Budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a restaurant in a nearby town on the return route — try slow-cooked lamb shank (kjöt) or fish of the day. Budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip — allow 8–10 hours. Roads may be icy in January; a 4WD vehicle is recommended. Check road conditions at road.is before departing. Dress in waterproof layers as Gullfoss can be very wet from spray.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the hotel. Enjoy a slow breakfast and use the hotel's spa or wellness facilities. Take a morning walk along the beachfront to watch the winter sunrise (around 11:00 in January) paint the sky in golden hues over the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool dating back to 1891. Soak in the naturally heated 38–40°C waters surrounded by small geysers and hot springs that bubble and steam around the pool. The rustic, authentic atmosphere makes this a memorable alternative to the busier Blue Lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a second opportunity for aurora viewing. January's long nights and the rural darkness around the Secret Lagoon area offer excellent conditions. The jeep guide will scout the best sky conditions and take the group to optimal viewing spots.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — try Icelandic skyr with berries and granola.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel or a nearby café before heading to Flúðir.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Minilik restaurant in Flúðir area or back at the hotel. Try Icelandic meat soup or grilled trout. Budget around 3,500–5,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is around 2,800–3,500 ISK per person — much more affordable than the Blue Lagoon. Bring a swimsuit, towel (available to rent), and flip-flops. The lagoon is open year-round and the steam rising from the surrounding hot springs is particularly atmospheric in winter. Flúðir is approximately 1–1.5 hours from the Reykjanes area.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast — drive east along Route 1 to explore Iceland's dramatic southern landscapes. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall, where you can walk behind the cascading curtain of water (may be partially icy in January — check conditions). Continue to Skógafoss waterfall for sweeping views from the top of the staircase.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara — one of the most dramatic beaches in the world, with towering basalt column formations (Reynisdrangar sea stacks) rising from the ocean. Walk along the volcanic black sand and admire the powerful Atlantic waves. Visit the nearby village of Vík for a warm drink and a look at the iconic hilltop church.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive west. Stop at Dyrhólaey promontory if light permits for panoramic coastal views. Return to the hotel for dinner and aurora watching from the beachfront if skies are clear.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before an early departure.
meals.lunch: Stop at a café in Vík — try a lamb soup or fish and chips at Suður-Vík restaurant. Budget around 2,500–4,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel restaurant — treat yourself to a slightly indulgent meal such as pan-seared lamb fillet or lobster bisque. Budget around 5,000–7,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: The South Coast drive is approximately 250–300 km round trip from the Reykjanes area. Allow a full day. Reynisfjara beach has sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean and stay behind the safety markers. Roads may be icy; check road.is. Sunset is around 16:30 in January.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavik city — take a morning drive or bus into Iceland's capital (approximately 45 minutes from the Reykjanes Peninsula). Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and take the elevator to the tower for panoramic city views. Walk the colorful streets of the old town and browse local design shops and bookstores.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Harpa Concert Hall on the waterfront — marvel at its geometric glass facade and explore the interior. Stroll along the Sæbraut coastal path to the Sun Voyager sculpture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) for an introduction to Icelandic history and Viking heritage. Entry around 2,500 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Reykjavik's vibrant dining scene for dinner before returning to the hotel. Optionally, check out a local bar or café for Icelandic craft beer. Return to the resort and monitor aurora forecasts for a potential late-night viewing session on the beach.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before heading to Reykjavik.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Reykjavik — try Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur for an iconic Icelandic hot dog (around 500–700 ISK) or a café lunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja for traditional Icelandic dishes. Budget around 2,000–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Reykjavik — try Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market) for mid-range Icelandic seafood, or Snaps Bistro for French-Icelandic fusion. Budget around 5,000–8,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavik is very walkable — wear comfortable waterproof boots. January evenings in the city are lively despite the cold. Free Wi-Fi is widely available. Consider picking up local souvenirs such as Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) from the Kolaportið flea market if it's open on weekends.

day_by_day.morning: Midway rest and spa day at the hotel. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Use the hotel's beachfront location for a brisk morning walk and photography session — January light creates stunning low-angle golden-hour effects even at midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local community geothermal swimming pool (sundlaug) — these are beloved Icelandic institutions where locals gather to soak and socialize in naturally heated outdoor pools. Entry is typically 1,000–1,500 ISK. A great way to experience authentic Icelandic culture away from tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — third opportunity for aurora viewing. With a week of experience, you'll know what to look for in the sky. The jeep guide will take the group to the darkest and clearest location available based on that night's forecast.

meals.breakfast: Extended hotel breakfast — take your time and enjoy the full spread.
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at the hotel or a nearby café — try an Icelandic lamb sandwich or skyr bowl.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant — try kjötsúpa (traditional lamb soup) or plokkfiskur (Icelandic fish stew). Budget around 3,500–5,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate slower day to recharge for the second half of the trip. January travel in Iceland can be physically demanding due to cold, wind, and long drives — rest days are important. Use this time to review photos, journal, or plan any last-minute bookings for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula — a full-day excursion to one of Iceland's most scenic regions, immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Depart early and drive north along the western coast. First stop: Gerðuberg basalt columns, a natural wall of perfectly formed hexagonal basalt pillars.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano at the tip of the peninsula. Visit Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal villages with their dramatic lava arch formations and bird cliffs. Walk the scenic coastal path between the two villages (approximately 2.5 km). Stop at Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and the historic shipwreck remains.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the return drive south. The peninsula road offers potential aurora viewing on the return journey through dark rural areas. Arrive back at the hotel late evening for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure.
meals.lunch: Stop at Café Bjargarsteinn in Hellnar or a café in Grundarfjörður for soup and bread. Budget around 2,500–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Late dinner at the hotel restaurant upon return. Budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is approximately 2–2.5 hours from the Reykjanes area — this is a long day of around 400 km total. Start as early as possible to maximize the 5–6 hours of daylight. The coastal road around the peninsula can be icy — check road.is. The area is known for local seal colonies at Ytri Tunga beach — worth a quick stop.

day_by_day.morning: Return visit or extended soak at the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) — after your first visit on Day 4, this second visit allows you to relax more deeply and appreciate the natural surroundings. Arrive when it opens to enjoy the pool in peaceful morning conditions with rising steam in the cold air.
day_by_day.afternoon: On the return from Flúðir, stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake — a striking red and green caldera filled with vivid blue-green water. Walk the rim of the crater (entry fee around 700 ISK) for panoramic views. Continue to explore the surrounding area including Skálholt Cathedral, one of Iceland's most historically significant religious sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a relaxed evening. Enjoy dinner and spend the evening watching for northern lights from the beachfront — by now you'll have developed a good eye for aurora conditions in the sky.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departing for Flúðir.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop near Kerið or Skálholt. Budget around 2,000–3,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant — try a grilled lamb chop with roasted root vegetables. Budget around 4,000–6,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Kerið crater is a quick 20–30 minute stop and very photogenic in winter with snow on the red volcanic rim. Skálholt Cathedral has a small museum and is free to enter. The combination of Secret Lagoon, Kerið, and Skálholt makes for a well-rounded and relaxed day without excessive driving.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula's geothermal landscape in depth — visit the Reykjanes Geopark, a UNESCO Global Geopark. Start at the Reykjanesviti lighthouse (Iceland's oldest lighthouse) on the dramatic lava peninsula tip. Walk the surrounding lava fields and observe the powerful ocean waves crashing against the volcanic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Seltún geothermal area in Krýsuvík — a colorful landscape of boiling mud pools, steaming vents, and sulfur-stained earth in vivid yellows, reds, and oranges. Walk the boardwalk trails through this otherworldly landscape. Continue to Kleifarvatn lake, Iceland's largest lake on the peninsula, with its mysterious dark waters and surrounding lava fields.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — final guided jeep tour of the trip. The Reykjanes Peninsula's remote volcanic landscape provides dramatic foreground scenery for aurora photography. Celebrate any successful sightings with the group.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or café stop at a nearby town — try a warm lamb soup or hot chocolate to warm up after the outdoor exploration.
meals.dinner: Special dinner at a slightly upscale local restaurant to mark the approaching end of the trip. Try Icelandic langoustine (humar) or slow-roasted lamb. Budget around 6,000–9,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Seltún is free to visit and the boardwalk makes it accessible even in winter. Stay strictly on marked paths — the geothermal ground is dangerously hot just below the surface. Kleifarvatn is known for its eerie atmosphere and is said to be slowly shrinking due to underground fissures from a 2000 earthquake. Bring a camera for the colorful geothermal landscapes.

day_by_day.morning: Final Blue Lagoon visit — book an early-morning slot for a luxurious farewell soak in the iconic geothermal waters. This time, consider upgrading to the Comfort or Premium package for an in-water massage or a sparkling wine experience. The morning light and steam rising from the blue waters creates a magical atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort and spend the afternoon relaxing on the beachfront, packing souvenirs, and enjoying the hotel's amenities. Take a final long walk along the Icelandic coastline, reflecting on the journey. Visit a local craft or souvenir shop to pick up lopapeysa wool sweaters, lava salt, or Icelandic schnapps (brennivín) as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the hotel's restaurant — celebrate the trip with a full Icelandic tasting menu if available, featuring local lamb, Arctic char, skyr dessert, and traditional rye bread. Watch for northern lights one final time from the beachfront after dinner.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the Blue Lagoon visit — the spa experience includes a drink on arrival.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Blue Lagoon's café or back at the hotel upon return.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at the hotel — splurge slightly on a multi-course Icelandic meal. Budget around 7,000–10,000 ISK per person for a special occasion dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon Comfort entry starts around 12,990 ISK and includes a towel, one drink, and a silica mud mask. Book well in advance as slots fill quickly. This is a good day to charge all camera batteries, back up photos, and organize luggage for the journey home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning exploration — take a sunrise walk (around 11:00 in January) along the beachfront for last photographs of the Icelandic coastline. Visit any nearby spots you may have missed during the trip, such as a local fishing harbor, a turf house museum, or a geothermal bakery where rye bread is baked underground using geothermal heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon at the hotel — enjoy the spa or pool facilities one last time. Pack remaining belongings and check out procedures. Have a final coffee or hot chocolate at the hotel bar while reviewing your favorite memories and photos from the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Optional final Northern Lights watch from the hotel beach — set an alarm for 22:00–02:00 if aurora activity is forecast. Alternatively, enjoy a quiet evening at the hotel with a good book, Icelandic craft beer, and the sound of the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite of Icelandic smoked salmon, skyr, and rye bread.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel — perhaps a bowl of fish soup and fresh bread.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at the hotel or a nearby restaurant — keep it simple and satisfying. Try a classic Icelandic hamburger or fish and chips. Budget around 3,000–5,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to decompress and absorb the final moments of Iceland before departure. Check your flight time for Day 13 and arrange your airport transfer in advance — Keflavik Airport is approximately 45–60 minutes from the Reykjanes area. Confirm transfer booking with the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland — wake up early for one last look at the Icelandic landscape. Enjoy breakfast at the hotel and complete check-out. Depending on your flight departure time, you may have time for a brief stop at a nearby geothermal hot pot or a final stroll along the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavik International Airport. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for check-in, security, and duty-free shopping. Pick up last-minute Icelandic souvenirs at the airport — Icelandic chocolate, lava salt, beauty products made from Blue Lagoon minerals, and local spirits make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Iceland — carry the memories of northern lights dancing over volcanic landscapes, the warmth of geothermal waters in the Arctic cold, and the raw, untamed beauty of one of the world's most extraordinary destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor the last Icelandic spread.
meals.lunch: Light meal at Keflavik Airport — several cafés and restaurants are available airside. Budget around 2,000–4,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Dinner on board the flight or at your connection airport.

day_by_day.notes: Keflavik Airport has excellent duty-free shopping — alcohol and cosmetics are particularly good value compared to in-town prices. Check baggage weight limits if you've purchased wool sweaters or heavy souvenirs. Leave a review for your hotel and any exceptional tour guides — it supports Iceland's local tourism community. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep
experiences.description: Join a small-group guided jeep tour into the dark countryside away from Reykjavik's light pollution to chase the Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to maximize your chances of witnessing the phenomenon. Hot chocolate and blankets provided.
experiences.location: Golden Circle & Þingvellir area, Southwest Iceland

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Book the Comfort package for towel, drink, and mask included. A bucket-list hot spring experience unlike any other.
experiences.best_time_of_day: Evening (for potential northern lights views overhead)

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool, dating back to 1891, surrounded by geysers and hot springs bubbling nearby. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this authentic geothermal pool sits in a stunning rural landscape and costs a fraction of the price.

experiences.name: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull
experiences.description: Strap on crampons and explore the dramatic ice formations, crevasses, and blue ice caves of Sólheimajökull glacier with a certified guide. Learn about Iceland's volcanic geology and climate change impacts while experiencing one of the country's most iconic landscapes up close.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant food scene and Viking heritage on a guided walking tour through the city center. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh-caught fish, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit Hallgrímskirkja church and the colorful old harbor district.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing at Keflavík International Airport, a private luxury transfer awaits to whisk you to Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy complimentary welcome drinks and a resort orientation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in and settle into your beachfront suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the dramatic Icelandic coastline to acclimate to the surroundings. Visit the resort's private thermal pool for a relaxing soak after the long journey.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — your first evening is perfectly timed for an expert-guided small-group jeep excursion into the dark Icelandic countryside, away from light pollution. Your guide will use real-time aurora forecasts to maximize sighting chances.

meals.breakfast: Onboard flight meal
meals.lunch: Welcome light bites and Icelandic smoked salmon platter at the resort's lounge upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dine at the resort's signature restaurant — try pan-seared Arctic char with dill cream and roasted root vegetables, paired with an Icelandic craft beer or fine Scandinavian wine

day_by_day.notes: January offers long dark nights — ideal for aurora hunting. Pack warm, layered clothing including thermal base layers, waterproof outer shell, gloves, and a hat. The jeep tour typically runs 21:00–01:00. Ensure your camera is charged and set for long-exposure night photography.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the resort. Afterwards, indulge in the resort's spa facilities — book a signature volcanic stone massage or a geothermal facial treatment using Icelandic mineral-rich products.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa — just a short luxury transfer from the resort, immerse yourself in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters. Upgrade to the premium Retreat Spa experience for in-water massages, silica mud masks, and exclusive access to the serene lava-surrounded pools.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour at the beachfront bar. Watch the last light fade over the North Atlantic before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Elaborate Scandinavian buffet at the resort — skyr parfaits, smoked lamb, rye bread, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — enjoy an in-water floating tray of Icelandic langoustine soup, lobster rolls, and sparkling wine while soaking
meals.dinner: Private chef's table experience at the resort — a curated 5-course tasting menu featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients such as reindeer tenderloin, langoustine, and skyr-based desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa package well in advance as slots fill quickly. Bring a waterproof hair tie and expect your hair to feel dry after the silica-rich water — complimentary conditioner is provided on-site.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — a private luxury version of the guided walking tour through Iceland's charming capital. Explore Viking heritage at the National Museum of Iceland, admire the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church, and taste your way through local delicacies at the city's finest artisan food stalls and boutique eateries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Browse Reykjavik's high-end boutiques along Laugavegur Street. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall for a self-guided architectural tour of its stunning geometric glass facade overlooking the harbor. Stop at a local gallery showcasing contemporary Icelandic art.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — a second opportunity to witness the aurora borealis. Your expert guide will take you to a new remote location based on tonight's solar activity forecast for the best possible viewing.

meals.breakfast: In-room gourmet breakfast delivered to your suite — freshly baked pastries, Icelandic honey, smoked salmon, eggs, and premium Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik — Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant offering a Nordic tasting menu with bold, seasonal flavors and local foraged ingredients
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik — a celebrated restaurant reinventing traditional Icelandic recipes with modern flair; try the salted cod head and lamb broth

day_by_day.notes: The walking tour is best done in the morning when shops and sites are freshest. Reykjavik's streets can be icy in January — wear grippy waterproof boots. Private car and driver available for the day to transfer between Reykjavik and the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak — depart early via private luxury vehicle for the charming Flúðir village in the Golden Circle region. Arrive at Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool before the day-tour crowds. Enjoy the intimate 38–40°C geothermal waters surrounded by steaming geysers and snow-dusted lava fields in near-solitude.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Golden Circle highlights with your private driver-guide: witness the explosive eruptions of the Strokkur geyser at Geysir, and marvel at the thundering Gullfoss waterfall — one of Iceland's most powerful cascades, especially dramatic in winter with ice formations along its edges.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Enjoy the resort's private outdoor hot tub overlooking the ocean under the stars — a perfect opportunity for another aurora sighting from the comfort of your own suite's terrace.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast — freshly squeezed cloudberry juice, skyr bowls with Icelandic honey, warm porridge, and eggs cooked to order
meals.lunch: Picnic luxury hamper prepared by the resort chef — artisan sandwiches with smoked lamb and pickled vegetables, thermos of hot Icelandic soup, and warm pastries enjoyed near Gullfoss
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Geysir — dine inside a working tomato greenhouse; their tomato soup and tomato-based cocktails are legendary and unique to Iceland

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is approximately 1.5 hours from the resort. Bring your swimsuit and a change of warm clothes. January daylight is limited (roughly 5–6 hours), so the Golden Circle tour should be timed to maximize the brief afternoon light.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Hike on Sólheimajökull — depart early with a private guide for the South Coast. Strap on crampons and a safety harness for an expert-led hike across the breathtaking Sólheimajökull glacier. Explore dramatic ice formations, electric-blue crevasses, and sculpted ice caves formed by centuries of glacial movement.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the South Coast with stops at the iconic Skógafoss and Seljalandsfoss waterfalls — in winter, these are often partially frozen and dramatically lit. Walk behind Seljalandsfoss for a unique perspective (weather and ice conditions permitting).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at the resort by early evening. Book a private in-suite couples' spa treatment — a volcanic mineral body wrap followed by a hot stone massage to soothe muscles after the glacier hike.

meals.breakfast: Early energy-boosting breakfast at the resort — protein-rich Icelandic skyr, smoked meats, rye bread, hard-boiled eggs, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Skál! Restaurant in Vík — a cozy South Coast gem offering fresh langoustine bisque and Icelandic lamb burger with hand-cut fries
meals.dinner: Resort's fine dining restaurant — pan-roasted duck breast with blueberry reduction, wild mushroom risotto, and a decadent skyr panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: The glacier hike requires a moderate level of fitness. All safety equipment (crampons, harness, helmet) is provided by the guide. Waterproof trousers and sturdy ankle-support boots are essential. The hike takes approximately 3 hours on the ice.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort. Enjoy a slow start with breakfast in bed, followed by a private yoga or meditation session arranged by the resort's wellness concierge — ideally conducted in a glass-walled studio overlooking the ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Reykjanes Peninsula with a private guide — visit the dramatic Bridge Between Continents (spanning the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates), the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pots, and the eerie volcanic lava fields of the peninsula.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — third opportunity for aurora viewing. Your guide will select a completely new dark-sky location based on updated forecasts. Enjoy complimentary hot chocolate and Icelandic schnapps under the stars.

meals.breakfast: In-room luxury breakfast — smoked salmon eggs Benedict, fresh fruit bowl with Icelandic berries, and a mimosa with sparkling elderflower
meals.lunch: Café Bryggjan in Grindavík — a classic Icelandic fisherman's café serving legendary lobster soup and fresh-caught fish of the day
meals.dinner: Private beachfront dinner arranged by the resort — a candlelit table set on a heated terrace with a curated 4-course menu and sommelier-selected wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjanes Peninsula is extremely geologically active — follow your guide's instructions carefully near hot spring areas. The Bridge Between Continents walk is short but exposed to wind, so dress warmly.

day_by_day.morning: Full resort spa day — begin with a sunrise dip in the resort's geothermal pool, then book back-to-back treatments: a deep-tissue massage, a volcanic clay body scrub, and a signature Icelandic facial using Arctic botanicals and glacial water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Helicopter scenic flight over Iceland's volcanic landscapes — arrange through the resort's concierge for a private helicopter tour over the Reykjanes lava fields, Þingvellir National Park, and the glittering coastline. A truly unforgettable aerial perspective of Iceland's raw beauty.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a quiet evening at the resort. Sip Icelandic craft spirits at the bar and watch for potential aurora activity from the resort's private beachfront observation deck.

meals.breakfast: Spa-appropriate light breakfast — green smoothie with Icelandic moss and spirulina, chia pudding, fresh berries, and herbal tea
meals.lunch: Resort poolside dining — a light but luxurious menu of smoked trout salad, avocado on dark rye, and freshly squeezed Icelandic juice blends
meals.dinner: Omakase-style sushi and Nordic fusion dinner at the resort's specialty restaurant — featuring Arctic shrimp, seaweed, and Icelandic salmon in beautifully crafted small plates

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent and should be booked with a flexible cancellation policy. The resort concierge can arrange this experience and will monitor weather conditions closely. Midweek is often less busy for spa bookings.

day_by_day.morning: Private snowmobile adventure on a glacier — arranged via the resort's concierge, this exhilarating experience takes you racing across the vast white expanse of Langjökull, Iceland's second-largest glacier. No prior experience needed; full safety briefing and equipment provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the man-made ice tunnel inside Langjökull glacier — walk through a carved tunnel deep inside the living glacier and learn about Iceland's glacial geology, climate history, and the mesmerizing blue ice formations.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a warm soak in the private suite's hot tub. Enjoy a nightcap of Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) while scanning the sky for the northern lights from your beachfront terrace.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast to fuel the active day — scrambled eggs with smoked lamb, hash browns, fresh bread, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: On-glacier warming station — hot Icelandic meat soup (kjötsúpa) and thermos of hot cocoa provided by the tour operator
meals.dinner: Fiskmarkaðurinn (Fish Market Restaurant), Reykjavik — renowned for its sushi-inspired Icelandic seafood; try the tuna tataki with Icelandic herbs and the lobster tempura

day_by_day.notes: Snowmobile tours typically require a valid driver's license. Dress in the warmest layers possible — windproof suits are provided over your clothing. The glacier ice tunnel tour is approximately 1 hour and requires comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Þingvellir National Park private guided tour — explore Iceland's most historically significant site, a UNESCO World Heritage landscape where the world's first parliament (Alþing) was established in 930 AD. Walk the dramatic rift valley between tectonic plates and learn about Iceland's Viking-age democracy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or dry suit diving in Silfra Fissure — the crystal-clear glacial water of Þingvellir offers one of the world's most unique dive experiences: swimming between two continental plates in water with 100-meter visibility. A private instructor guides you safely through this extraordinary underwater world.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Jeep — Þingvellir's remote dark skies make it an exceptional aurora-viewing location. Your guide may combine the evening drive with a stop here for optimal conditions.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast — Icelandic waffles with skyr and crowberry jam, fresh orange juice, and a pot of Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Þingvellir National Park Visitor Center café — warm lamb soup and rye bread with Icelandic butter
meals.dinner: Grillið at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavik — a rooftop restaurant with panoramic city views offering premium Icelandic lamb rack and a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: The water temperature in Silfra is approximately 2–4°C year-round — a dry suit is mandatory and provided. No prior diving experience is required for snorkeling. Minimum age is typically 12 years. The experience is breathtaking but physically demanding due to the cold.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning — sleep in and enjoy breakfast at the resort. Take a slow walk along the black sand beach near the resort, collecting sea glass and watching the dramatic winter waves of the North Atlantic crash against the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private whale watching tour (winter season) — board a luxury vessel from Reykjavik or Keflavík harbor for a guided marine wildlife excursion. January offers chances to spot humpback whales, minke whales, white-beaked dolphins, and seabirds. Heated indoor cabin and expert marine biologist guide onboard.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a cultural evening in Reykjavik — attend a classical music concert at the stunning Harpa Concert Hall, home to the Iceland Symphony Orchestra. Pre-arrange premium seats through the resort concierge.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet — smorgasbord of Nordic cheeses, cured meats, fresh pastries, fruit compotes, and specialty Icelandic herbal teas
meals.lunch: Onboard whale watching vessel — premium packed lunch of smoked salmon wraps, Icelandic cheese, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Apotek Restaurant, Reykjavik — a stylish restaurant in a former pharmacy offering creative modern Icelandic cuisine; try the lamb shank with root vegetable purée and the skyr cheesecake

day_by_day.notes: Winter whale watching has slightly lower sighting guarantees than summer, but the dramatic winter seascape and fewer tourists make it a premium experience. Dress in full windproof gear on deck — the sea wind is biting in January.

day_by_day.morning: Private ice cave exploration in Vatnajökull — depart early via luxury 4x4 for the Vatnajökull glacier region (approximately 4–5 hours from the resort). These natural ice caves, accessible only in winter, reveal stunning crystalline blue ice chambers sculpted by glacial meltwater. A private glaciologist guide leads the exclusive tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon — witness the ethereal floating icebergs drifting from Europe's largest glacier into the lagoon. In winter, the lagoon is often partially frozen and dusted with snow, creating a hauntingly beautiful landscape. Nearby Diamond Beach features ice chunks washed ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stay upgrade: check into a luxury lodge near Vatnajökull (arranged by resort concierge) — a glass-ceiling suite or aurora cabin for direct northern lights viewing from your bed.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — energy bars, fruit, yogurt, and takeaway coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Café — warm lamb soup and freshly baked bread overlooking the glacier lagoon
meals.dinner: Fosshotel Glacier Lagoon Restaurant — a remote luxury hotel near the lagoon offering a seasonal menu of local fish, lamb, and Icelandic dairy-based desserts

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are weather and safety dependent — your guide will assess conditions on the day. Helmets and crampons are provided. This is a long day (12+ hours of travel and activities) — comfortable, warm layering is critical. The overnight glacier lodge experience is one of the trip's highlights.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up in the aurora cabin — if the skies were clear overnight, enjoy a final morning of potential northern lights viewing from your glass-ceiling suite. Enjoy a peaceful breakfast surrounded by Iceland's remote eastern wilderness before departing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic drive back along the South Coast — stop at Skaftafell Nature Reserve for a short hike to the Svartifoss waterfall, framed by dramatic basalt columns. Continue westward with stops at the Eldhraun lava field moss landscape and Dyrhólaey arch (weather permitting).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort. Celebrate your penultimate evening with a private champagne toast on the beachfront terrace. Indulge in a final northern lights hunt from the resort's observation deck with a glass of Veuve Clicquot.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the glacier lodge — freshly baked croissants, Icelandic honey, smoked meats, and French press coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stop at Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a beloved local café serving homemade lamb soup and Kleina (Icelandic twisted doughnuts)
meals.dinner: Resort's premium fine dining — a celebratory farewell feast: Icelandic lobster bisque, grilled lamb chops with truffle jus, and a decadent dark chocolate lava cake with skyr ice cream and a bottle of Grand Cru Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Vatnajökull back to the resort is approximately 4–5 hours. Plan departure from the glacier lodge by 09:00 to make the most of the limited daylight hours for South Coast stops. Keep your camera ready throughout the drive — the scenery is extraordinary.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy a long, luxurious farewell breakfast at the resort. Take one last dip in the geothermal pool and a slow walk along the beachfront. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight departure time, make one final stop at the Blue Lagoon Comfort package for a relaxing pre-flight soak (the lagoon is conveniently located between the resort and Keflavík Airport). Freshen up in their premium changing facilities before heading to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport. Check in for your departure flight with memories of Iceland's fire and ice that will last a lifetime.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — the full Nordic spread: smoked fish, artisan cheeses, warm pastries, Icelandic pancakes with cloudberry jam, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Lava Restaurant at the Blue Lagoon — a fitting final Icelandic meal of langoustine soup and open-faced smoked salmon sandwich
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or onboard flight dining

day_by_day.notes: Confirm Blue Lagoon booking in advance and select the Comfort or Premium package which includes a towel, one drink, and silica mud mask. Allow at least 2.5 hours at the lagoon before needing to depart for the airport. Keflavík Airport is approximately 20 minutes from the Blue Lagoon. Duty-free at the airport is excellent for Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and wool products.
